title: Article I, section 1: legislative vesting
summary: Article I vests the legislative powers granted by the Constitution in Congress.
notes:
The nondelegation debate asks what follows from the constitutional allocation of legislative power to Congress. The Gundy plurality regards substantial implementing discretion as compatible with that allocation when Congress supplies an intelligible principle. Gorsuch’s dissent would identify legislative policy choices more restrictively and permit detail-filling, conditional fact-finding, and assignments of nonlegislative responsibilities.

The allocation of legislative power and the inquiry into what qualifies as legislative are separate steps. The assigned opinions agree that Congress cannot simply transfer its legislative responsibility but disagree about how to characterize the disputed authority. The separately assigned text of Articles I–III is on file (added-sources/US Constitution.pdf), linked above.
